sections.h2: Where a Crawford County deed is recorded
sections.html:
The Crawford County Recorder's office in Bucyrus, the county seat, records every deed in the county. It serves as the official land records office for all real estate here, and its number is 419-562-6961. Staff follow sections 317.11 and 317.112 of the Ohio Revised Code, which control how a document must look before it is accepted.

One local step catches sellers off guard. A document that transfers real estate must be approved before it is filed, and that approval begins at the Crawford County Engineer's office, not at the recorder. Staff there cannot offer legal advice, which is why an attorney or title agency should draft the deed. Fill-in-the-blank forms exist, but whoever submits one is responsible for meeting every legal requirement.

Senate Bill 94 added $5 to recording costs starting January 1, 2025. Today a standard deed costs $39 for pages one and two, then $8 for every further page, and a printed side is one page. Reference fees of $4 and the office's formatting standards still apply on top.

A few other charges can turn up in a sale. Recording the release of a lien costs $4, a federal tax lien filing costs $5, and each marginal notation on a document adds $4 to the regular fee. Plats and condominium drawings are charged by size: $0.10 per square inch, minimum $40 a page. When you go in, bring separate checks for the recorder, the auditor and the treasurer.

sections.h2: What the recorder wants to see on a deed
sections.html:
The recorder publishes an eleven-point checklist. Sellers most often trip on these:

  • An original document, signed and notarized
  • A prepared-by statement on any deed drawn up in Ohio
  • The complete legal description, which the office uses to index the deed by location
  • Book and page references to earlier recordings, in any later document
  • Clear labels on every exhibit and schedule
  • The preparer's name and address, a return address and a phone number for minor corrections
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope, so the original comes back without postage charges

Pages must be legible enough to scan, and that is the filer's responsibility. Check the work again before you go, fees especially, since a miscount is a common reason for rejection.

The office indexes by legal description, not street address. If all you have is a house number, find the owner name and transfer date on the Crawford County Auditor's search page first, then bring that to the recorder.

sections.h2: What the Crawford County Auditor adds to a sale
sections.html:
The auditor decides the value your tax bill is based on and receives the conveyance paperwork. Property is revalued every three years under Ohio Department of Taxation rules, and tax is figured on 35% of market value. Crawford County has 54 taxing districts, each with its own rate. An owner pays no more than 10 mills of unvoted levies, and the voted portion depends on local elections.

At a sale, the buyer files a value statement under section 319.202, and the seller pays the conveyance fee plus any transfer tax the commissioners have levied under section 322.02. The conveyance fee in section 319.54 is $1 or 10 cents per $100, whichever is greater. State law caps any county transfer tax at 30 cents per $100, and the auditor can tell you the local rate.

Other auditor rules a seller may run into:

  • A value complaint goes to the Board of Revision, with the filing window running January 1 to March 31.
  • New construction or an improvement over $2,000 has to be reported, and skipping that can bring a 50% penalty on the owner's taxes.
  • Building permits come from the cities of Bucyrus and Galion, Jackson, Jefferson and Polk townships, and the villages of Crestline, New Washington, North Robinson and Chatfield.
  • Farmland in the current agricultural use program pays a one-time $25 enrollment fee.
  • A manufactured home buyer has 30 days to register with the auditor or face a $100 penalty.

North central Ohio's Crawford County has two cities, Bucyrus (the largest) and Galion. Population was 42,025 in 2020 and is estimated at 41,896 for July 2025. In 2020, 65.9% of residents lived in urban areas and 34.1% in rural ones, which helps explain why a Bucyrus lot and a township farmhouse can be priced so differently.

The typical owner-occupied home is worth $136,700 on the 2020 to 2024 figures, with 73.1% of homes lived in by their owners. Median gross rent is $794. Just 3 building permits were counted in 2025, which means buyers mostly shop among existing houses. A written cash offer or a local appraisal prices a specific house better than a countywide median. Sellers in Galion, Crestline, Bucyrus and the townships all record at the same Bucyrus office.

sections.h2: What is the order of steps for a seller?
sections.html:
The trip has three stops. First comes the Crawford County Engineer's office, where the transfer is approved. Second comes the auditor, who receives the buyer's value statement and the seller's conveyance fee. Last comes the recorder, who accepts the finished deed, collects the page-based fee and indexes the document by its legal description.

Because each office wants a separate payment, carrying three checks saves a second trip. If the deed is going by mail, include the stamped return envelope and a contact number so staff can phone about a small fix instead of rejecting the package. Questions about which stop comes next can go to the recorder at 419-562-6961, though staff will not draft documents or advise on legal wording.

sections.h2: Settling liens and taxes before you go
sections.html:
The recorder records liens but does not release them. Property tax matters belong to the Treasurer, and court filings belong to the Clerk of Courts. Before the deed is filed, a seller should sort out the following with the right office:

  • Ask the County Treasurer for the unpaid tax figure, so the title company can pay it from the proceeds.
  • Ask the lender to file a release of any old mortgage, since the recorder only records it.
  • Check with the Clerk of Courts for judgments tied to the owner.
  • Ask the County Engineer's office about the transfer approval step.
  • Match the legal description to the one on your last deed.

The same steps apply when the buyer pays cash and takes the house as-is. A cash sale can close faster, but the title still has to be clear, and a missed release can hold up the filing.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Crawford County Recorder?
faqs.a: The office number is 419-562-6961. The office is in Bucyrus.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a three-page deed in Crawford County?
faqs.a: The fee table shows $47.00 for three pages. That is $39 for the first two pages and $8 for the third, before any other charges the document triggers.

faqs.q: Does the recorder remove liens from my title?
faqs.a: No. The office records certain liens but does not release them. Property tax liens go through the County Treasurer, and court matters through the Clerk of Courts.

faqs.q: Where does the transfer process start in Crawford County?
faqs.a: At the County Engineer's office. A document that transfers real estate has to be approved there before it moves on.

faqs.q: Can I search records by street address at the recorder?
faqs.a: Not directly. The recorder indexes by legal description, so look up the owner name or transfer date on the County Auditor's search page if you only have an address.
